When to use

These classes are the column's spacing, not components with a surface. None mints a value: 24, 12 and 8 are --len-24, --len-12 and --len-8. The argument is the ratio — a gap between two different questions has to be clearly larger than the gaps inside either one. --zones is spent on five pages: rate, rate-aerial, rate-inspection, support and role-select. .dr-stack--zones is on account-edit and operator-profile-setup; .dr-main--center on switch-role alone. A sixth modifier, .dr-main--fab on account, operator-account and wallet, pads the column's foot for the floating action. The fifth rung, .dr-rail--zone (margin-block 12 around the progress rail), is documented with the progress rail.

There is no WCAG criterion for spacing; this is the proximity rule, and the check is a ratio either way. No heading is added between zones: the boundary is spatial, and every row already names itself.

role-select: the copy that asks and the fork that answers are two zones: 24 between them against 8 inside the list, 3:1.

Don’t

I need a service done I provide services

--zones used to space the cards of one list. Two answers to one question now sit as far apart as two questions. Put them in a list, whose gap is the space between cards. On a form whose groups are panels, use .dr-stack--zones at 12, not --zones at 24.
